title: Samson
summary: Nazirite of Dan, son of Manoah; judged Israel twenty years "in the days of the Philistines" and died pulling down the house of Dagon (Judg 13–16).
description: Added with the judges-period records from James B. Jordan's chronology (secondary display).

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (F. N. Jones): 1151 BC (no higher-tier year available). Jordan (secondary display) never sets the sort.

birth.date: "PROBABLE BIRTH 1151 BC" ("MAXIMUM YEARS FOR SAMSON = 68: 1169 BC")
birth.citation: Jones, Chart No. 4 "Judges to the First 3 Kings" (© 1993 Floyd Jones; chart text revised "As of 2007"), Samson life-line
birth.note: Jones, 15th ed. (2002), ch. V p. 86: birth "near the end of the 18 year Philistine and Ammonite oppression"; "1140 is a viable alternative".

birth.date: 2849b AM, 1155 BC ("As foretold by the angel, Samson the Nazarite was born at Zorah")
birth.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Fourth Age §380 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

birth.date: "2861 - ... Likely births of Samson, Samuel, Obed, and Jephthah's daughter."
birth.citation: Jordan, From Creation to Solomon (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2, Biblical Horizons, Oct. 2001), ch. 11 "The Era of the Judges and the Reign of Saul", p. 52
birth.note: 2001 revision. Jordan's 1991 list (BC 3:8) has an earlier year; see the second Jordan entry. p. 40: "The Philistine oppression lasted 40 years (Judges 13:1). Samson was born about this time." Judges (1985) p. 237: Samson conceived "About the time the Philistine bondage began" (no year). Judges (1985), ch. "Samson the Nazirite", pp. 237-238: "About the time the Philistine bondage began, God appeared to the mother of Samson, and she conceived"; "When Samson was about 20 years old, God began to stir him up ... about the time of the battle of Aphek". Intervals only; that book states "it is not possible to construct a strict chronology for the book of Judges" (p. 55).

birth.citation: Jordan, "Chronology and Kings (II)," Biblical Chronology 3:8 (August 1991), section "The Judges", summary list
birth.note: 1991 scheme, superseded by Jordan himself in 2001 (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2 dates the whole judges sequence 26 years later because he there ends the 300 years of Judg 11:26 when Ammon took the villages, AM 2860, not at Jephthah's victory).

death.date: "BC 1121 – 20 = 1101 BC (Year Samson died & Samuel succeeded him)"
death.citation: Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), ch. V "Chart Four", p. 86
death.note: Samson's 20-year judgeship 1121–1101 BC (Chart No. 4: "SAMSON ... HE JUDGED 20 YEARS DURING THE 40 YEAR PHILISTINE DOMINION").

death.date: 2887c AM, 1117 BC (dies in the temple of Dagon, "when he had judged Israel for 20 years")
death.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Fourth Age §384 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

death.date: "2901 - Death of Samson, battle of Mizpah, deliverance from Philistine oppression."
death.citation: Jordan, From Creation to Solomon (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2, Biblical Horizons, Oct. 2001), ch. 11 "The Era of the Judges and the Reign of Saul", p. 52
death.note: 2001 revision. Jordan's 1991 list (BC 3:8) has an earlier year; see the second Jordan entry. Samson's judgeship begins 2881 ("Death of Eli, beginning of ... Samson's judgeship in the South"). p. 40: "his 40 years seem to be the same as those of the Philistine oppression."

death.date: "2875 - Death of Samson, battle of Mizpah ..."
death.citation: Jordan, "Chronology and Kings (II)," Biblical Chronology 3:8 (August 1991), section "The Judges", summary list
death.note: 1991 scheme, superseded by Jordan himself in 2001 (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2 dates the whole judges sequence 26 years later because he there ends the 300 years of Judg 11:26 when Ammon took the villages, AM 2860, not at Jephthah's victory).
